title: unable to get local issuer certificate when deploying from VS Code
msgKeys: unable to get local issuer certificate
symptom:
The deploy fails with a TLS certificate error, typically "unable to get local issuer certificate" or "self signed certificate in certificate chain".

Common with on-premise systems using an internal corporate certificate.
rootCause: Not verified on our own systems. Node.js does not trust a certificate issued by an internal CA because that CA is not in Node's default trust store.

solutions.label: Register the internal CA with Node.js
solutions.body:
Get the corporate CA file from IT, then:

  export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/company-ca.pem
  npm run deploy

Windows PowerShell:
  $env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="C:\path\company-ca.pem"

This is the correct fix: TLS verification stays fully in place, you only add a CA you trust.

solutions.label: Disable certificate checking (local DEV only)
solutions.body:
In ui5-deploy.yaml:

  configuration:
    strictSsl: false

Do NOT use this on CI/CD or any shared environment, and do not commit it to the main branch — it switches off server identity verification entirely.

prevention: Distribute the internal CA file and the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS instruction as part of onboarding, instead of leaving each developer to disable strictSsl on their own.
